column1: # Javanese Latin ⟨e⟩ lexicon — CROSS-SCRIPT TRANSFER (the Punjabi Gurmukhi↔Shahmukhi pattern). The Latin ⟨e⟩ is
# ambiguous: pepet /ə/ vs taling /e/~/ɛ/ are BOTH written ⟨e⟩ and unrecoverable from Latin orthography (no rule).
# The Aksara Jawa script writes them with distinct signs (pepet ꦼ vs taling ꦺ), so it is MORE phonemic.
# PROVENANCE: each Aksara word (kaikki jav Aksara, Wiktionary human) was transliterated to its Latin form
# (deterministic — Aksara→Latin collapses pepet/taling→⟨e⟩, exactly the ambiguity) and phonemized via our OWN
# Aksara front-end (aksara.ts, which resolves ⟨e⟩); the resolved pronunciation is pinned to the Latin key. Pinned
# only where the Latin default (⟨e⟩→ə) DIFFERS — i.e. the taling words the Latin path gets wrong (pangeran→paŋeran,
# bebek→bebeʔ). Overrides the SHIPPED Latin path only; phonemizeWordRules (and the referee eval) bypass it. The
# referee eval FOLDS ⟨e⟩ (əɛe→e), so this is a shipped-quality gain the folded % cannot see.
